name: Ekai Chin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only documentation read (ISO 639-3 CR 2018-017 PDF): an unpublished 2016 LSDO sociolinguistic survey (wordlist/RTT), no phonology or stress description of Laoktu/Ekai Chin.

sources.citation: So-Hartmann, Helga. 2009. A descriptive grammar of Daai Chin (STEDT Monograph 7). Berkeley: UC Berkeley. pp. 25-26 (Southern Chin subclassification)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog's subclassification source for the Ashoic / Sumtu-Laoktu node; describes Daai, not Läoktü, so it cannot supply an Ekai stress statement but is the nearest full grammar in the South Peripheral group for a family-level default.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2025. Change Request 2025-035: Ekai Chin [cey] update name to Läoktü Chin (adopted, effective 2026-07-15). Submitters U Thar Nyunt (Läoktü Literature and Culture Committee), C. & N. Statezni (SIL), Mang Tial Khun & Paing Nan (LSDO)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Confirms the documentation gap: 'There is very little published literature about the Läoktü Chin community. In the only published article about the Läoktü Chin community and its language that we know of to date, the name Läoktü Chin is used.' (p. 2). Names Ekai, Kholai, Daitü, Khamo (Khamaw) as dialects; cites only Statezni et al. 2023 and the unpublished LSDO 2016 survey report.

sources.citation: Statezni, Carey; Nathan Statezni; Paing Nan; Abraham; Mang Tial Khun. 2023 [issue Vol.17 No.4, 2024]. Sociolinguistic Survey of the Chin Speech Varieties Spoken along the Dalet Stream, Ann Township, Rakhine State, Myanmar. Asia Social Issues 17(4): e264779, 27 pp. DOI 10.48048/asi.2024.264779
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (462-item wordlists, RTT, interviews, dialect mapping); sections are Introduction / Context and literature review / Methodology / Findings / Conclusions / Recommendations, no phonology and no wordlist appendix. Only prosodic mention: RTT subjects said other varieties differ 'in tones and vocabulary' (p. 9-11 of PDF, lines 399, 472). States (p. 2): 'The language varieties along the Dalet Stream are undocumented in the literature.'

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2018. Change Request 2018-017: adopted create [cey] Ekai Chin (2019-01-25), with New Code Request form 2018-017_cey
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexical-similarity and RTT figures vs Asho, Uppu, Cumtu (Sumtu), Laitu; autonym Ekai [ʔe kai], alternate name Lawktu; 'Sino-Tibetan, Tibeto-Burman, Kuki-Chin-Naga, Kuki-Chin, Southern, Asho-related'; published sources = only the unpublished LSDO Survey Team 2016 manuscript; written literature 'none'.

sources.citation: Any phonological description of the nearest sister language Sumtu Chin [csv, sumt1234] (Glottolog cites Justin Watkins 2013: 79 for subclassification) or of Asho Chin [csh]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Ekai shares 76% lexical similarity with Sumtu and 76-81% with Asho; a sister-language prosody description would be the closest proxy, but would not be a statement about Ekai itself and should not enter the catalog under ekai1234.
